cells.tense: The compass is true in your hand and you are actually reading it now.
cells.act: collect the fruit of the patient wait
cells.ask: Set aside twenty minutes with a long effort you've kept up. Put down what it actually made — the hours, the skill, the piece that held. Leave the note where you'll pass it this week.
cells.core:
You know what's fair without needing to work it out, and it lands clean — what you owe, what's owed you, where the line sits. Aiming at what you want to become, the reading is straight, and the aiming and the reading don't fight each other. Nothing is being tallied in the dark.

The upkeep is the price, and it's being paid. What this balance can feed next is gathering, so take a thing you've carried a long while and count what it grew — the skill, the hours, the part that held. Set the count somewhere you'll see it. What you get is proof that your patience paid, in your own hand, needing nobody's confirmation.
cells.sheetLine: The compass reads true, and the aim holds.
cells.verb: Weighing what is fair with an inner compass
cells.place: Where you aim at what you actually want to become

cells.tense: You are scoring what has not happened yet, and the pen is pressing hard.
cells.act: hold someone else up with what you have
cells.ask: Think of someone near you who's worn thin. Carry one real thing for them this week and finish it — a meal, an errand, an hour on what they're stuck on.
cells.core:
You reach for what you want to become and the fairness-sense turns judge — futures audited before they arrive, who will deserve what, what the cost will be to whom. Pulled at what's still light, you keep calculating whether you'll have earned your place there, whether it's fair to want it. The accounting is private, and it runs well past the moment it was supposed to guard.

Shared strength is the way back: a hold that lifts something instead of weighing it. Rather than pre-tallying who will owe what, take someone whose hands are full and help carry it, once, to done. Holding something up settles the compass faster than counting does, and afterwards you'll see how much of the ledger was imaginary.
cells.sheetLine: You are ahead of your life, settling scores that don't exist.
cells.verb: Weighing what is fair with an inner compass
cells.place: Where you aim at what you actually want to become

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that is already behind you.
cells.act: point to the passage you can see
cells.ask: Pick a person stuck in something you already got through. Point at the one way through you'd take — a sentence, a phone call, whatever it is. Then leave it with them.
cells.core:
Ask what's fair and the answer comes back quiet, or you wave the question off. Aiming at what you want has thinned to almost nothing, and the pull toward light doesn't feel like yours to follow. You stand where something finished a while back, holding a fairness-sense that still works but has nothing to measure.

The compass comes back through a path it once walked. Take one person in the middle of something you already came through. Point at the way you'd go — no coat pulled over it, no managing. That's the whole act. Saying the route out loud is the missing proof you found it: direction that lands in you by leaving you.
cells.sheetLine: The door is behind you. Your compass still works.
cells.verb: Weighing what is fair with an inner compass
cells.place: Where you aim at what you actually want to become

cells.tense: The compass is steering and your hand is on it, unnamed.
cells.act: list the pulls on you and mark which are yours
cells.ask: Take a sheet and list what's pulling at you right now — the course, the plan, the should. Beside each, mark whether it started with you or arrived from somewhere else. Change nothing yet.
cells.core:
The fairness-sense is awake, and how you weigh things runs clean without you standing beside it — the instinct for what's owed, the flinch at what isn't. Aiming at what you want to become, you already keep to a line: these moves are right, those are not, and in your own account you simply see it.

Give that an edge before it goes back to steering unseen. Take one pull you're following and trace where the pull came from — your own want, or a borrowed one you can't place. Put the answer beside it. You aren't deciding anything on this trail: just letting the compass hear its own name once.
cells.sheetLine: What reads as instinct is a fairness you chose.
cells.verb: Weighing what is fair with an inner compass
